fields.description:
# S2 — Capability decisions read `ModelProfile`, not provider-name strings

## Context / Problem

Two capability decisions are made by string-matching a provider name. `src/rebar/llm/structured.py:63`
`output_mode()` picks `NativeOutput` only when the prefix is in `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS`
(`structured.py:46`, a frozenset of four literal names), and `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:341` attaches prompt-cache
settings only when the resolved string starts with `anthropic` (via `anthropic_model._anthropic_cache_settings`,
`anthropic_model.py:39`). Both are wrong for Bedrock-hosted Claude, whose capability flags differ from the
direct Anthropic API — the model string would say `bedrock`, so caching would silently switch off and
structured output would silently take the prompted path. PR #121 hit exactly this and patched it with a
`force_prompted: bool` threaded through four call sites.

## Approach

pydantic-ai exposes a per-vendor capability record at `model.profile` (`ModelProfile`). Replace both string
matches with profile reads, and add a rebar-side override layer for cases upstream gets wrong or does not
cover — using `ModelProfile` overrides for Bedrock-hosted Anthropic is the documented upstream guidance
precisely because those flags diverge from the direct API.

### Where the code lives (resolves the S1 `providers.py` size conflict)

`capabilities_for()` and the override table go in a **new leaf module `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py`**, NOT in
`providers.py`. Reason: S1 (`7468-25e5-ae4f-43d1`, closed) carries an **attested** acceptance criterion that
`providers.py` stays under 300 LOC, and it is already 225 LOC — adding the record, the override table and the
cache-settings selector would breach a criterion that has been signed. Capability *interpretation* is also a
distinct concern from provider *construction*, and the repo's module-size policy targets 200–500 LOC units
split along existing seams. `capabilities.py` is a leaf on the same footing as `anthropic_model.py`: it imports
nothing from `runner` or `providers`, and heavy libraries are imported inside functions.

### The capability record

`capabilities_for(model) -> ModelCapabilities` returns a small frozen dataclass with **three** fields:

- `native_structured_output: bool`
- `prompt_cache_style: str` — one of `"none"` / `"anthropic"` / `"bedrock"`
- `supports_thinking: bool`

**The exact `ModelProfile` fields read** (verified against the pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.1):

- `native_structured_output` is derived from `ModelProfile.supports_json_schema_output` (the strict
  json_schema capability `NativeOutput` requires). `ModelProfile.supports_json_object_output` and
  `ModelProfile.default_structured_output_mode` also exist and are NOT used — named here so a reader knows the
  choice was made, not missed.
- `prompt_cache_style` is derived from the profile's **capability FIELDS**, not from a name string and — for
  the Bedrock arm — not from its concrete type either: a profile exposing `bedrock_supports_prompt_caching`
  yields `"bedrock"`; an `AnthropicModelProfile` yields `"anthropic"`; anything else yields `"none"`.

  **Why field presence rather than `isinstance(profile, BedrockModelProfile)`** — this is a hard constraint, not
  a style choice. `BedrockModelProfile` is exported ONLY from `pydantic_ai.models.bedrock`, which imports
  `botocore` at module top; there is no SDK-free `pydantic_ai.profiles.bedrock` (verified: the `profiles`
  package has no `bedrock` submodule). `boto3` appears in `pyproject.toml` only under the `reviewbot` extra, so
  the CI env that runs `make test` does NOT have it. An `isinstance` check would therefore (a) break the
  stdlib-only `import rebar.llm` contract and (b) fail in CI. Field presence needs no vendor import.
  `AnthropicModelProfile` is safe to `isinstance` against because `pydantic_ai.profiles.anthropic` is SDK-free.

  **S2 must add NO new runtime dependency** — in particular it must not add `boto3`/the `[bedrock]` extra, which
  is S3's scope.
- `supports_thinking` is derived from `ModelProfile.supports_thinking`. (`ModelProfile.thinking_always_enabled`
  and `thinking_tags` also exist and are not read here — the record answers "can this model reason at all",
  not how its reasoning is delimited.)

### How the profile is obtained — the lazy-model-string problem S1 created

`capabilities_for()` cannot simply read `model.profile`, because after S1 (`7468`, closed) **`run()` does not
always hold a model OBJECT.** S1 deliberately leaves a provider that pydantic-ai recognizes but rebar does not
build (openai, google) as a lazy model **string**, because eagerly resolving it would force that vendor's
optional SDK to be importable — `pydantic_ai.providers.openai` raises `ImportError: Please install the openai
package` and rebar's `[agents]` extra deliberately does not install it (verified: the `openai`, `google` and
`groq` SDKs are all absent from the venv).

So `getattr(model, "profile", None)` on a `str` returns `None`, which would hit the conservative fallback and
set `native_structured_output=False` for OpenAI and Google — silently destroying their `NativeOutput` path.
`tests/unit/test_structured.py:177` asserts against exactly that, so it would surface as a regression.

`capabilities_for(model_or_model_string)` therefore accepts **either** form:

1. an object exposing `.profile` (the rebar-built providers: Anthropic, and Bedrock in S3) -> read it directly;
2. a provider-qualified model **string** -> resolve the vendor's profile WITHOUT constructing a provider, via
   a single `_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` map from provider name to the matching function in **`pydantic_ai.profiles.*`**;
3. anything else -> the conservative record + one WARNING.

The critical verified fact that makes (2) work: **`pydantic_ai.profiles.*` are pure capability records and
import cleanly WITHOUT the vendor SDK** — `from pydantic_ai.profiles.openai import openai_model_profile`
succeeds and returns `supports_json_schema_output=True` with no `openai` package present, unlike
`pydantic_ai.providers.openai`. So rebar reads capabilities for a provider it cannot construct, which is exactly
the asymmetry S1's lazy-string path needs.

`_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` is a **single registry table**, and it is the one place a provider name maps to anything.
The epic's criterion forbids *scattered* provider-selection branches and requires name->behaviour mapping to
live in one registry; this is that registry, not a reintroduction of `startswith("anthropic")` decision-making.

**The required key set, enumerated.** A missing key silently falls back to the conservative record, which is a
behavior change, so the keys are specified here rather than left to the implementer. Every row below was
resolved against pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.1:

| key | resolver | `supports_json_schema_output` | why the key is needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | `profiles.anthropic.anthropic_model_profile` | True (overridden to False) | direct Claude |
| `openai` | `profiles.openai.openai_model_profile` | True | in today's `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` |
| `openai-chat` | `profiles.openai.openai_model_profile` | True | upstream also exposes this prefix |
| `google-gla` | `profiles.google.google_model_profile` | True | **the prefix rebar itself emits** — `_PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX` maps `google`/`google_genai` -> `google-gla` |
| `google-vertex` | `profiles.google.google_model_profile` | True | in today's `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` |
| `vertexai` | `profiles.google.google_model_profile` | True | deprecated alias upstream still accepts |
| `google` | `profiles.google.google_model_profile` | True | upstream's CURRENT name |
| `google-cloud` | `profiles.google.google_model_profile` | True | upstream's current name for Vertex |
| `groq` | `profiles.groq.groq_model_profile` | **False** | in today's `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` |

Two things this table settles:

- **`google-vertex` does NOT change behavior.** It is enumerated explicitly, and `google_model_profile` reports
  `supports_json_schema_output=True` for it, so it keeps `NativeOutput`. (Note `google-gla`/`google-vertex`/
  `vertexai` are *deprecated aliases* in 1.107.1 — upstream's live prefixes are `google`/`google-cloud` — but
  rebar's own `_PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX` still emits `google-gla`, so omitting the aliases would break rebar's own
  output. S1's `providers._DEPRECATED_PROVIDER_ALIASES` exists for the same reason.)
- **groq remains the ONLY disclosed behavior change**, and it is a property of its profile, not of a missing key.

`bedrock` is deliberately absent: it is a rebar-BUILT provider (S3), so it arrives as a model object and takes
the `.profile` path. Adding a string resolver for it would need `boto3` importable, reintroducing exactly the
optional-SDK coupling this design avoids.

### `supports_thinking`'s processing protocol — who reads it, and who does not

This field's consumer is **provenance, not control flow**, and that distinction is the whole protocol:

- **`output_mode()` does NOT read it.** It keeps taking the caller-supplied `thinking: bool`, because pairing
  extended thinking with a native/forced output constraint is a documented Anthropic **400 on the request** —
  a property of the *call being made*, not of the model's capability. Reading the profile here would answer the
  wrong question.
- **S5 (`343b-4fdc-6722-469b`) reads it**, and reads it as part of the whole record: S5's signed provenance
  payload is `{provider, model, endpoint_host, tier, capabilities}` where `capabilities` **is this record**. So
  every field on this dataclass becomes part of a *signed, non-repudiable* verdict artifact.

That last point is why `supports_thinking` belongs on the record now rather than being deferred to the story
that first branches on it. rebar does **not** currently persist the model's chain of thought, so a verdict's
reasoning is not recoverable after the fact. If chain-of-thought retention becomes a requirement — a plausible
auditability ask for a gate that blocks merges — the signed record must already state whether the model that
produced each historical verdict was *capable* of thinking, because that fact cannot be reconstructed later
from the sidecar. Adding the field after S5 ships is also strictly more expensive: it changes the shape of an
already-signed payload rather than being present from the first signature. The field is therefore load-bearing
for audit, and it is a deliberate, documented exception to "no field without a consumer" — the consumer is S5,
one story away in this same epic, and it is named here.

### The rebar override table — schema, lookup, precedence, and its one entry

The override layer is **load-bearing, not speculative**, and the reason is concrete. Verified against pinned
pydantic-ai 1.107.1: `anthropic_model_profile("claude-opus-4-8").supports_json_schema_output` is **`True`**, and
so is Bedrock-hosted Claude's. A naive profile read would therefore set `native_structured_output=True` for
Claude and flip `output_mode()` to `NativeOutput` — silently changing rebar's PRIMARY provider away from the
`PromptedOutput` path that `structured.py:40-46` deliberately chose (pydantic-ai may still route strict
json_schema through ToolOutput per profile, and PromptedOutput plus rebar's tolerant parse is the reliable
combination). `tests/unit/test_structured.py:179` already asserts Claude gets `PromptedOutput`. The override
table is what keeps that contract.

**Schema.** An ordered tuple of `(predicate, overrides)` pairs — deliberately NOT a dict keyed by provider
name, for two reasons: a name key would reintroduce exactly the string matching this story exists to remove,
and it could not express the single rule below, which must span two different *hosts* of the same model family.

```python
_REBAR_OVERRIDES: tuple[tuple[Callable[[ModelProfile], bool], Mapping[str, object]], ...] = (
    (_is_claude, {"native_structured_output": False}),
)
```

- **Predicate**: `Callable[[ModelProfile], bool]`, reading the profile's **type** and/or its **capability
  fields**. It never inspects the model string or the provider name.
- **Value**: a partial mapping of `ModelCapabilities` field name -> value. Only the named fields are replaced;
  unnamed fields keep their profile-derived value.
- **Lookup**: iterate in declaration order; the **first** matching predicate wins and iteration stops. No
  merging across multiple matches, so there is no precedence ambiguity to reason about.
- **Precedence vs the profile**: overrides are applied **after** profile derivation (including after the
  `prompt_cache_style` type-dispatch), so an override always wins over the upstream flag.

**The one initial entry** identifies Claude on either host:

```python
def _is_claude(profile: ModelProfile) -> bool:
    """Direct-Anthropic OR Bedrock-hosted Anthropic."""
    return isinstance(profile, AnthropicModelProfile) or (
        getattr(profile, "bedrock_thinking_variant", None) == "anthropic"
    )
```

Both arms are required and neither is redundant: **Bedrock-hosted Claude's profile is a `BedrockModelProfile`,
NOT an `AnthropicModelProfile`** (verified — they are sibling `ModelProfile` subclasses), so an
`isinstance(AnthropicModelProfile)` test alone would miss the very models this epic exists to support, and
Bedrock Claude would wrongly get `NativeOutput`. The second arm reads pydantic-ai's own
`BedrockModelProfile.bedrock_thinking_variant` field, which is `'anthropic'` for Bedrock Claude, `'openai'` for
Bedrock-hosted OpenAI, and absent/`None` for Meta and Amazon models (all verified). Note this is a **capability
field read whose value happens to be a string enum** — materially different from
`resolved.startswith("anthropic")` on a model string, which is the pattern this story removes.

**A rule derived purely from flags was tried and rejected.** `supports_json_schema_output and not
supports_thinking` looks elegant and reproduces Anthropic and OpenAI correctly, but it was tested against every
provider in today's `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` and **breaks two**: `gemini-2.5-flash` has
`supports_thinking=True` (would lose `NativeOutput`) and `groq` has `supports_json_schema_output=False` (same).
So `native_structured_output` is derived from `supports_json_schema_output` alone, plus this table.

**One disclosed behavior change: groq.** `groq_model_profile(...).supports_json_schema_output` is `False`, yet
today's hardcoded `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` includes `groq`, so groq currently gets `NativeOutput` and after
this change gets `PromptedOutput`. This is accepted deliberately rather than papered over with a second
override entry: the profile is the authoritative capability source (the entire premise of this story), groq is
not reachable through rebar's own provider map (`_PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX` covers anthropic/openai/google only), no
test asserts it, and the direction is the safe one — `PromptedOutput` works everywhere. A test pins the new
behavior so it is deliberate rather than incidental.

### Cache-settings selection — ONE function, one shape

`_anthropic_cache_settings(resolved: str)` is **deleted** from `anthropic_model.py` and replaced by a single
`cache_settings_for(caps: ModelCapabilities)` in `capabilities.py`, which dispatches on
`caps.prompt_cache_style`. This is a definite decision, not a choice left to the implementer: one function with
one calling convention, so `runner.py`'s call site has exactly one shape.

**The exact settings keys** (verified against pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.1 — note
`BedrockConverseModelSettings` does **not** exist; the class is `BedrockModelSettings`):

| `prompt_cache_style` | class | keys set |
|---|---|---|
| `"anthropic"` | `pydantic_ai.models.anthropic.AnthropicModelSettings` | `anthropic_cache_instructions=True`, `anthropic_cache_tool_definitions=True` |
| `"bedrock"` | `pydantic_ai.models.bedrock.BedrockModelSettings` | `bedrock_cache_instructions=True`, `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions=True` |
| `"none"` | — | returns `None` (no cache keys sent) |

`AnthropicModelSettings` additionally has `anthropic_cache_messages` / `anthropic_cache` and
`BedrockModelSettings` has `bedrock_cache_messages`; none of them are set here, preserving today's behavior
exactly (only the instructions + tool-definitions breakpoints).

### Degradation contract

A model whose `.profile` is missing, `None`, or of an unrecognized type degrades to the **conservative** record
(`native_structured_output=False`, `prompt_cache_style="none"`) and logs **exactly one** WARNING naming the
model type. Conservative because both fallbacks are the safe direction: `PromptedOutput` works everywhere, and
sending no cache keys is always valid. It never raises — an unknown provider must not break a run.

**Alternative rejected:** PR #121's `force_prompted` boolean. It is a per-call-site patch that grows one
argument per capability per provider, and it encodes the answer at the caller rather than at the model — the
next provider needs another boolean threaded through the same four signatures.

**Rollback.** The change is behavior-preserving for both currently-shipping providers, so backing out is a
revert of this single change; there is no data migration and no config flag to unwind. If a profile read
misbehaves in production the conservative fallback is already the safe state (prompted output, no cache keys),
which degrades cost/latency but never correctness.

## Scope

Production:

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` (**new** leaf) — `ModelCapabilities`, `capabilities_for()` (accepting a
  model object OR a model string), the `_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` registry, the rebar override table, and
  `cache_settings_for()`.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` — `output_mode()` (`:51`) takes a `ModelCapabilities` instead of a model
  string; delete `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` (`:46`) and its use (`:63`).
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — **three** edit targets:
  - `:28` — the module-level `from rebar.llm.anthropic_model import (...)` block currently pulls in
    `_anthropic_cache_settings`. Since that helper is deleted, this import must drop it and instead import
    `cache_settings_for` (and `capabilities_for`) from `rebar.llm.capabilities`. Leaving it would be a hard
    ImportError at module load, not a subtle failure.
  - `:341` — the cache gate (the plan previously mis-cited `:316`, which is the toolset-filter line) reads
    `prompt_cache_style` via `cache_settings_for()`.
  - `:599` — the `output_mode()` call site passes the capability record instead of the model string.
- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — **delete** `_anthropic_cache_settings` (`:39`) and its docstring
  reference (`:10`).

Tests — **all four** affected files (S1 shipped with an under-enumerated test scope; this is the complete set,
established by grepping every call site):

- `tests/unit/test_llm_capabilities.py` (**new**) — the mapping + degradation + cache-settings selection +
  `supports_thinking` derivation and its non-consumption by `output_mode()`.
- `tests/unit/test_structured.py` (`:176`, `:177`, `:179`, `:189`) — four `output_mode()` calls using the old
  string signature; must move to capability records.
- `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` — **both** cache tests, not just one:
  `test_cache_settings_enabled_only_for_anthropic` (`:310`, plus the direct `_anthropic_cache_settings` import
  at `:17` and its four calls at `:313`–`:319`) and
  `test_cache_model_settings_attached_only_for_anthropic` (`:358`).
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` (`:90`) — monkeypatches
  `runner_mod._anthropic_cache_settings`; that patch target disappears, so it must move to the new seam. (This
  fourth site is the same file whose `_build_retrying_anthropic_model` patch S1 had to fix — it stubs
  `pydantic_ai` empty, so its replacement must not force a real settings-class import.)

## Testing

Unit tier for the mapping (a pure function over a profile) plus contract tier for the two consumers, since the
defect class is a consumer reading the wrong signal.

- happy path: an Anthropic model yields `prompt_cache_style == "anthropic"` and `output_mode` returns
  `PromptedOutput`; an OpenAI model yields `native_structured_output=True` and `NativeOutput`.
- **Bedrock case (the motivating defect), in two layers so it runs without `boto3`:**
  1. **Always-run:** a profile stub carrying the Bedrock capability fields (`bedrock_supports_prompt_caching`,
     `bedrock_thinking_variant="anthropic"`) yields `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` AND
     `native_structured_output=False` (the Claude override reaching its Bedrock arm). No AWS, no credentials,
     no optional SDK.
  2. **`boto3`-gated pin (the verified-fake guard):** a test skipped via `importorskip("boto3")` asserts the
     REAL `BedrockProvider.model_profile("us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-...")` actually exposes those same
     fields with those same values. This is what stops layer 1 from drifting into a fake that passes while real
     Bedrock breaks; it runs locally and in S3's env even though CI skips it.
  `cache_settings_for()` for `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` returns a `BedrockModelSettings` with
  `bedrock_cache_instructions` and `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions` both `True` — i.e. caching is ON for
  Bedrock-hosted Claude, exactly what silently switched off before. That assertion is also `boto3`-gated,
  because constructing `BedrockModelSettings` requires the import.
- edge: `thinking=True` forces `PromptedOutput` regardless of profile (existing contract, must not regress).
- failure path: a model whose profile is missing/`None`/unrecognized degrades to the conservative record
  (`native_structured_output=False`, `prompt_cache_style="none"`) rather than raising, and logs exactly one
  WARNING (asserted with `caplog`, including that it is one record, not per-call spam).
- contrast case: `test_cache_model_settings_attached_only_for_anthropic` is rewritten to assert by capability
  rather than by provider name, and still shows cache settings absent for a non-caching model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rn '_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS' src/ tests/` is empty
- [ ] `grep -rn 'force_prompted' src/ tests/` is empty — no `force_prompted`-style boolean is added to any
      signature (this is the proving command)
- [ ] `grep -rn '_anthropic_cache_settings' src/ tests/` is empty — the string-gated helper is gone, replaced
      by the single `cache_settings_for()` seam
- [ ] `output_mode()` accepts a `ModelCapabilities` record, and its tests assert `NativeOutput` for a native
      provider, `PromptedOutput` for Anthropic, and the `thinking=True` override
- [ ] a test asserts a Bedrock-hosted Claude model yields `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` and that
      `cache_settings_for()` returns `BedrockModelSettings` with `bedrock_cache_instructions` and
      `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions` set — the Bedrock cache path has an executable proof, constructed
      offline with no AWS credentials
- [ ] a test asserts an unknown/missing profile produces the conservative record AND exactly one WARNING log
      record
- [ ] `supports_thinking` is on the record, derived from `ModelProfile.supports_thinking`, asserted `True` for a
      thinking-capable Anthropic model and `False` in the conservative fallback — and a test asserts
      `output_mode()` does NOT consult it (a thinking-capable model with `thinking=False` still gets
      `NativeOutput` when its profile supports json_schema), so the provenance field cannot silently become a
      control-flow input
- [ ] the override table is an ordered `(predicate, overrides)` tuple whose predicates read only profile TYPE
      and profile FIELDS — `grep -n 'startswith' src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` is empty — and a test asserts
      **both** arms of the Claude rule: a direct `AnthropicModelProfile` AND a Bedrock-hosted Claude profile
      (a `BedrockModelProfile` with `bedrock_thinking_variant == "anthropic"`) each yield
      `native_structured_output=False`, while Bedrock-hosted Meta/Amazon profiles do NOT match the rule
- [ ] a test pins the disclosed groq change (`PromptedOutput` where it was `NativeOutput`), so it is deliberate
      rather than an accidental regression, and tests confirm `openai` and `google-gla` still get `NativeOutput`
- [ ] `capabilities_for()` accepts a model STRING as well as a model object, and a PARAMETERIZED test asserts
      that every key in `_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` resolves a real profile off the lazy-string path — specifically
      that `openai:gpt-4o`, `google-gla:gemini-2.5-flash`, `google-vertex:gemini-2.5-flash` and
      `google:gemini-2.5-flash` all yield `native_structured_output=True` — proving profiles are read WITHOUT
      the `openai`/`google` SDKs installed and that the conservative fallback is NOT reached for a provider
      rebar merely defers. A test also asserts no key in today's `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` is dropped from
      the resolver table except the deliberately-disclosed `groq`
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` imports nothing from `runner` or `providers`, and `providers.py` stays
      under the 300 LOC that S1's attested criterion fixed
- [ ] S2 adds NO new runtime dependency: `git diff pyproject.toml` shows no `boto3`/`[bedrock]` addition, and
      the whole capability path works with `boto3` ABSENT — `import rebar.llm` still pulls in no heavy module
- [ ] the Bedrock capability assertion runs WITHOUT `boto3` (field-stub layer), and a separate
      `importorskip("boto3")` test pins that stub's fields against the REAL
      `BedrockProvider.model_profile(...)`, so the stub cannot silently drift from reality
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the FULL gating suite (`make test`, not just `tests/unit`) pass
